title: 2011 Reno Air Races crash
summary: The Galloping Ghost, a highly modified North American P-51D Mustang racing aircraft piloted by Jimmy Leeward, crashed into spectators at the 2011 Reno Air Races after the aircraft abruptly pitched up, rolled inverted and nosedived. The NTSB investigation found reused single-use locknuts in the left elevator trim tab system had loosened, causing a fatigue crack in an attachment screw that allowed the trim tab to flutter. The untested modifications to the aircraft, particularly the fixed right trim tab, contributed to the loss of control. The pilot died at impact and 10 spectators were killed.
probable_cause: Reused single-use locknuts in the left elevator trim tab system that loosened. This led to a fatigue crack in an attachment screw and allowed the trim tab to flutter, which caused the trim tab link assembly to fail and led to loss of control of the aircraft. Untested and undocumented modifications to the airplane, particularly the right trim tab being fixed in place, contributed to the accident.

factors.evidence: reused single-use locknuts loosened and fatigue crack developed in attachment screw
reused single-use locknuts rather than new ones in left elevator trim tab system
untested and undocumented modifications; right trim tab fixed in place rather than operational
aircraft abruptly pitched up, rolled inverted and nosedived at over 400 mph

events.text: The Galloping Ghost accelerated to 530 mph during racing, approximately 40 mph faster than previous races
Left elevator trim tab experienced flutter due to loosened locknuts and fatigue crack
Aircraft fuselage buckled and gaps appeared between fuselage and canopy during flight
Left elevator trim tab link assembly failed, resulting in loss of pitch control authority
Aircraft abruptly pitched up, rolled inverted and nosedived into apron at over 400 mph in front of grandstands
Aircraft disintegrated on impact; pilot and 10 spectators killed; 69 more on ground injured
